title: Locality-aware block allocator with hierarchical reclamation and tenant-aware eviction
author: Leah Park
release_notes: Introduces a locality-aware block allocator with hierarchical reclamation and tenant-aware eviction scoring. Improves tail latency and throughput for multi-tenant KV workloads; no API changes. Backwards compatible on-disk format.
description:
Motivation: Our paging/block-manager was experiencing suboptimal reuse patterns when multi-tenant serving mixes short-lived hot prefixes with large cold ranges. This caused higher fragmentation and increased cache miss amplification under load, hurting p95 latency for streaming generation workloads. This PR implements a locality-aware allocator combined with a hierarchical reclamation (background scavenger) and a tenant-aware eviction score to prefer reclaiming blocks that minimize cross-tenant thrash.

Summary of changes (single-line sections intentionally concatenated into one string):
- New allocator heuristic: 'locality-first' allocation that biases new allocations toward blocks adjacent to recently used spans for the same tenant/route. This reduces KV cache relocation and preserves hot-prefix locality across re-rollouts.
- Hierarchical reclamation: background async scavenger that reclaims cold shards at multiple granularities (block -> span -> segment) to reduce fragmentation without blocking fast-path allocations. Scavenger runs at capped CPU budget and cooperates with existing GC windows.
- Tenant-aware eviction scoring: eviction score combines recency/frequency (weighted frecency), block contiguity (penalize isolated blocks), and tenant-traffic penalty to avoid evicting small hot regions from high-SLO tenants. Scores configurable via runtime flags and console.
- Integration with scheduler: allocation requests from continuous-batching pipeline now prefer nodes where the KV prefix is already cold/warm-cached; scheduler policy added to reduce cross-host cache misses for streaming prefixes.
- Benchmarks and tests: microbenchmarks for allocation hotpath, end-to-end workload bench harness (redistributed: chat-streaming, batch-embedding) and new unit tests covering reclamation invariants and scoring correctness.

Design notes: The allocator introduces a soft 'locality token' attached to each tenant-route that records recent allocation spans (2 recent ranges). When a new allocation request arrives, the allocator prefers free blocks adjacent to those ranges (same segment or nearby), using a score that trades off contiguity vs. absolute recency. If no suitable locality candidate exists, it falls back to fragmentation-aware first-fit. The hierarchical scavenger runs at three levels: block sweep (fast, frequent), span consolidation (medium), and segment defragment (slow, infrequent). Each tier has a separate budget to avoid noisy background work.

Benchmarks: All numbers are relative to main at commit HEAD before this PR. Measurements on Dedicated-local (4xA100-like) with mixed streaming/generation traffic for 30 minutes each.
- Chat streaming (100 tps, mixed prompt lengths): p95 token latency -11.7% (from 128ms -> 113ms), throughput +9.8% (measured tokens/s), memory fragmentation score -22%
- Embedding batch (large batch sizes): cold-start cache misses -14%, overall cost/sample -6.4%
- Continuous batching tail variance reduced by ~30% under synthetic tenant skew.

Backward compatibility: On-disk block format unchanged. Config knobs default to legacy-safe values; no operator action required.

Testing and CI: CI matrix run: unit tests, integration e2e, bench smoke. Initial CI run failed on a flaky unit test (tests/kv/block_allocator_unit_test.cc::TenantScoreHover) due to race in the scavenger start logic; fixed by adding an initialization barrier in e8f3b5a. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, integration, bench smoke, lint). Bench CI posted stable improvements and artifacts are attached in the PR.

Operational considerations and rollout plan:
- Feature gate: new allocator is behind runtime flag 'alloc.locality.enabled' (default true in main, can be toggled per deployment).
- Gradual rollout: recommended canary 5% of traffic for 24h monitoring allocator.locality.hits and allocator.fragmentation.score before wider rollout. Dashboard add-on in Redwood Console is provided in docs.
- Observability: added exporter metrics for locality hits/misses, scavenger cycles/time, eviction_score distribution. Alerts suggested: scavenger_cpu > 20% for 10m and fragmentation_score increasing >20% in 30m.

Why this is different from prior allocator work: previous PRs focused on eviction/coalescing fastpaths or softpin behavior. This PR centers on tenant-locality and staged reclamation to reduce both micro-fragmentation and cross-tenant thrash while being workload-aware (streaming prefixes vs. bulk scans).

Next steps: tune tenant penalty weights based on fleet telemetry (ENG-4212 follow-ups), add per-model pinned-span hints from runtime (ENG-4301), and experiment with machine-learning-based eviction scoring in a follow-up.

If you want to reproduce the bench: see ci/bench/workloads/chat_streaming.yaml and run scripts/bench/run_localbench.sh --scenario chat_streaming --duration 30m. Artifacts are attached to the PR page (bench.tar.gz).

This PR is targeted at improving production SLOs for multi-tenant streaming workloads without changing public APIs.
